text:
mika: Repro for a nasty onboarding hiccup: unzipped redwoodctl on Windows, double-clicked from Explorer, ran `redwoodctl login`. Browser auth finished but CLI still said not-logged-in after restart.
alex: sounds like the temp-profile thing. What does `redwoodctl profiles list` show?
mika: two profiles: default -> C:\Users\mika\.redwood and default-2 -> C:\Users\mika\AppData\Local\Temp\tmp-rwd-42. The token ended up in the temp one.
nirav: new wrinkle: when we run the binary from a Temp extraction path the CLI uses a fallback config dir. That makes the browser callback write tokens to ephemeral storage.
sam: mitigation ideas: detect BIN path in %TEMP% at startup and print a clear warning: "You're running from a temporary folder. Move the binary or use the installer." Also prefer persistent user config if present.
taylor: could we auto-migrate the token when we detect temp -> persistent? e.g., `redwoodctl migrate --from <tmp> --to default` with an interactive confirmation and a noninteractive safe default for CI.
mika: that would have saved a new hire a lot of pain. Also worth adding a Quickstart blurb: "If you used the zip, move the binary to a stable location before logging in."
nirav: I'll add a telemetry event installer.temp_profile_fallback and a startup banner. Migration CLI + tests next sprint. Sam — can you add Windows unzip scenario to QA matrix?
sam: yes — automation will unzip to Downloads and exercise login + migrate. We'll also add a unit test to normalize paths in `profiles list --json`.
alex: docs action: short troubleshooting note for "completed browser auth but CLI not logged in" with the migration command and how to check `profiles list`.
mika: security note: ensure migration copies tokens atomically and removes the temp copy.
taylor: approving plan. small UX win but avoids a ton of support tickets.
sam: creating ticket IN-4521 for banner + telemetry, IN-4522 for migrate CLI.
mika: thanks — verified the staging banner locally after mv-ing binary; feels much clearer. :white_check_mark:
